prompt:
Repaint this sprite sheet of a 2D narrative game in a different brush technique. The first reference image is the finished sheet of the character facing the viewer: keep its layout exactly, six figures in two rows of three, every pose, the size and place of every figure, the feet of each row on the same baseline. Figure one stands relaxed; figures two to four wave with the raised arm exactly as in the reference (arm out to the side, paw up and outwards, paw up and inwards); figure five is figure one with both eyes closed (each eye a short curved dab of the brush); figure six is figure one with the mouth open as if speaking. Only the painting technique changes, plus one costume detail: as in the walking figures of the second reference, a dark grey satchel hangs on its strap at the hip on the right side of the picture, partly behind the body and below the elbow, while the pale parcel stays where it is, under the arm on the left side of the picture; the strap runs across the chest. The second reference image is the same character already painted in the right technique: copy its brush, its washes, its ink tones, the vermilion scarf and its level of detail exactly, so that both sheets belong to the same game. The third reference image is a study sheet of brush marks: same brush, but do not copy its content. The fourth reference image only shows the costume and the proportions: do not copy its drawing style, its colours or its layout.

Painting technique: boneless ink painting (mokkotsu), the East Asian way of painting figures and animals without outlines: every shape exists only as a wet wash of ink laid with the side of a soft brush; there are no contour lines at all, nowhere a thin even line around a shape or between two shapes. The dark fur of the arms, the legs, the back of the head and the eye stripes is one or two broad, wet strokes of dark ink each, uneven in density, with visible bristle streaks, darker where the ink pooled, and soft feathered edges that bleed a little into the paper, here and there broken into dry-brush streaks with flecks of white paper. The cap is one medium-dark grey wash, the vest one medium grey wash, the satchel one dark grey wash, the parcel one very pale grey wash; each wash is slightly uneven and has a slightly darker rim where it dried. The shirt, the white face stripes and the belly are bare paper: they are defined only by the washes next to them; where a white shape meets the background there is at most a soft pale grey wash on its shadow side, never a line. The scarf is one wet wash of vermilion red, darker where the wash pooled, with three or four quick flicks of the brush tip for the fringe. Eyes and nose are single dabs of black ink; buttons and buckles at most tiny dabs. All colours of the costume description are translated into ink tones: the dark green cap and vest become grey ink, the brown satchel dark grey ink, the brown parcel pale grey ink, the cream shirt bare paper; the only colour is the vermilion scarf. No outlines, no pen lines, no fur texture, no knitted pattern, no hatching, no smooth gradients, no highlights. The same brush, the same ink tones and the same level of detail in every figure. Not a clean illustration, not a cartoon or mascot drawing with outlines, not a vector graphic, not a 3D render, not a watercolour in many colours.

The badger courier: an original mascot character, a stout, short-legged badger with a broad black-and-white striped face, wearing a dark green peaked cap with a brass button, a dark green vest with pockets over a cream shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long red knitted scarf, a brown leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and a brown paper parcel tied with string under one arm.

The figures are isolated on a fully transparent background: everything outside the figures is transparent; the bare paper inside each figure (shirt, white face, belly) is opaque white. No paper texture or paper colour outside the figures, no ground line, no shadow on the floor, no seal stamps, no text.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.
